title: CLR/108/2017 of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd Vs Smt. Vindhya Sharma AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CLR No. 108 of 2017
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
None
Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Having heard the learned
counsel of the revisionist, it transpires
that trial of MACP 174/2012 ëVindhya
Sharma vs. Ashwani Kumar & Othersí
is undergoing in the court of Addl.
District Judge, Dehradun.
The order dated 09.01.2017
manifests that Insurance Company
wanted to summon the competent
authority who has control over
issuing/renewal of the driving licence
in the office of DTO, Hoshiarpur
(Punjab), wherefor, the learned court
also strived inasmuch as issued the
bailable warrant to the tune of Rs.
10,000/- to ensure the presence of
such Authority or any Competent
Officer/Official in his/her behalf but,
such warrant could not be executed.
So, the insurer (Opposite party no. 3 in
the Trial Court) was constraint to move
the application before the Addl.
District Judge to recourse the coercive
measures as contemplated under
Order 16 Rule 10 of the CPC.
Meanwhile, the court of Addl.
District Judge was manned by another
Judge, who refused to recourse such
means.
The Courts are sustain the
majesty of the law. The Addl. District
Judge would not have been hesitant to
recourse the coercive measures as

indicated above inasmuch as issuing
the arrest warrant of such Authority, if
he is not showing honour to the
process of the court.
In view of what has been set
forth above, the impugned order dated
01.6.2017 is hereby set aside. The
application 665 B moved by the
Insurance Company shall stand
allowed and the Addl. District Judge
will issue an appropriate order as
indicated above inasmuch as writing
letter to D.G.P. Punjab to ensure the
execution of process of the court.
The revision finally stands
disposed of.
